name: Lock-Free DeliveryQueue Subscriber Count

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

primaryTarget: native release build, criterion benches (macOS arm64)
hypothesisMarkdown:
## Lock-Free DeliveryQueue Subscriber Count Hypothesis

### Hypothesis

`DeliveryQueue::has_subscribers` locks the queue mutex; every `Signal` write calls it under the signal lock (experiment 10 measured ~20 ns per call). Mirroring the subscriber count into an atomic, updated under the queue lock whenever an entry is added or removed, answers it with one load and keeps the publisher/subscriber ordering argument (a subscriber registers before it snapshots under the publisher's lock).

### Scope Lock

**Tested mechanism:** atomic mirror of the subscriber count read by `has_subscribers`.
**Allowed changes:** `crates/src/primitives/delivery.rs` (shared state struct holding the mutex and the counter).
**Forbidden in this experiment:** new callers of `has_subscribers`, drain/enqueue lock changes, Signal changes.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
### Measurement Plan

Focused tests: `primitives::tests`, `primitives::delivery`, scalar tests (`tests`, `scalar_tests`) and full lib (DeliveryQueue is shared by everything); clippy/fmt. Bench `hot_paths` scalar-hot, `reactive_complexity`, `delivery_complexity` vs base. Pass: `signal-set-*` >=10% faster, no regression >10% elsewhere.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
### Expected Outcome

Signal writes ~5-15 ns cheaper.

**Passed Status**: false — Reverted failure. Next: keep the counter in the same allocation as the queue mutex so subscriptions capture one Weak as before.

### Scope Lock

**Tested mechanism:** tests pass; signal-set-no-subscribers -27% and signal-set-one-subscriber -9% (reproduced in two reruns; one +97% outlier was noise), but the subscribe-heavy delivery-queue-fanout bench regressed +6..+15% over three runs (mean ~10% at 32/256 subscribers): the counter lives in a second Arc, cloned into every subscription.
**Out-of-scope changes:** none.
